title: Binary control pulse optimization for quantum systems
contribution: A relax-round-improve framework for binary quantum control with SOS1 and switching constraints: penalized GRAPE or TV-regularized ADMM for the relaxation, SUR/CIA rounding with an extended SUR error bound, and a trust-region approximate local-branching improvement step.
problem_entry: Application-driven: GRAPE/CRAB handle only unconstrained continuous controls, while gate/QAOA settings need binary bang-bang controls with one active control and side constraints; B&B too slow, genetic algorithms poor (pp. 2-3).
key_idea: Squared L2 exact penalty keeps GRAPE usable for SOS1; TV regularizer solved by ADMM; SUR or CIA rounding (min-up-time, max-switching); trust-region MILP local branching with ared/pred test (pp. 10-19).
assumptions: F differentiable (p. 4); uniform piecewise-constant discretization (p. 4); Theorem 3 needs F bounded and DQCP feasible (p. 11); penalty exactness only for binary controls, cited from Sinclair 1986 (pp. 11-12).
proof_devices: Proposition 1: lower bound showing SUR fails without SOS1 in the relaxed control (p. 13)
Theorem 4: Sager's SUR bound extended by an additive (2N-1)/N*eps(dt) term (p. 13)
Corollary 1: eps(dt) <= sqrt(t_f * l * dt) ties penalty residual to rounding error (p. 13)
Theorem 3: l <= 2C_F/rho by contradiction against a feasible point (p. 34)
experiments: NEOS baselines with versions and time limits on energy minimization q=2,6 (Table 2, p. 20); 12 instances in four classes (Table 3, p. 22); theory-validation plots (Figs. 6, 8, 9, pp. 22-24); objective vs TV scatter (Fig. 12, p. 27); code on GitHub (p. 22).
positioning: Extends Vogt-Petersson trust region to constrained binary control and builds on Sager's SUR/CIA and Leyffer-Manns TV trust region [69] (pp. 2, 16, 18).
writing: Four numbered contributions (p. 3); a framework figure and an acronym table (p. 8); closing advice by user goal (p. 27).
limits_future: No global optimality for ADMM (p. 17); parameters need fine-tuning (p. 27); future: switching-time optimization and running time evolution on quantum hardware (pp. 25, 28).

method_links.note: Mixed-integer optimal-control toolkit (SUR/CIA, trust-region local branching of Leyffer-Manns) carried into quantum pulse design.
Baselines named with versions and limits, but no baseline tuning reported, one problem class, and a broad 'cannot solve' conclusion; closing advice is a rule by goal (step 5).
Proposition 1 shows the known SUR guarantee fails once its SOS1 hypothesis is dropped, before an extended bound is proved.

Plot each theoretical bound against the measured quantity as dt or rho varies (Figs. 6, 8, 9, pp. 22-24).
Report an objective-vs-switching scatter before and after the improvement step and recommend a method per user goal (pp. 26-27).
Integer trust-region radius schedule: halve above a threshold, then decrease by one (Algorithm 3, p. 19).

quotes.text: We show that as long as the violation of the SOS1 constraint is small, the solution that is constructed via SUR still satisfies the strong convergence properties of SUR.
Both cases require the use of the approximate local branching algorithm to improve final solutions.

title: On convergence of binary trust-region steepest descent
contribution: Under a compactness assumption on the gradient borrowed from CIA theory, binary trust-region steepest descent (BTR) produces binary iterates converging weakly-* to stationary points of the continuous relaxation; experiments confirm near-optimality and show a regularizing effect exploited by a coarse-SUR + BTR hybrid.
problem_entry: Theory gap: BTR known only to reach eps-stationarity, unlike CIA which has stationary limits under compactness (p. 2).
key_idea: Import CIA's assumption (grad J weak-norm continuous) and show BTR's termination quantity is the primal-gap criticality measure, so binary iterates converge weakly-* to stationary points of (R) (pp. 3, 8-9).
assumptions: Assumption 1.1: J bounded below, Frechet differentiable on L1, grad J Lipschitz L1->L2 and weak-norm continuous (p. 3); {0,1} values and no regularizer for concise presentation (pp. 1-2).
proof_devices: criticality measure C equals the L1 norm of min{g,0} at characteristic functions (Proposition 4.3, p. 8)
for {-1,0,1}-valued steps the L2 norm is the square root of the L1 norm (p. 11)
liminf C = 0 by contradiction on a vanishing radius (pp. 11-12), then lim via [35, Theorem 6] over successful steps (p. 12)
weak lower semicontinuity of C under compactness (p. 13); weak continuity of J by mean value theorem (Proposition 2.1, p. 5)
experiments: One 2-D elliptic tracking problem, 256x256 mesh: relaxation, CIA (SUR, COR, SHG) and BTR from three starts compared on objective, gap, time, iterations, interface length (Table 1, p. 17); mesh-refinement and hybrid tables (pp. 17-18).
positioning: Positions BTR [10] beside CIA [20, 28] and closes the theoretical gap between them; mentions SIMP as the topology-optimization alternative (p. 2).
writing: Standing assumptions stated up front with a remark on their domain (p. 3); unexplained observations flagged as such (p. 15).
limits_future: BTR slower than CIA (p. 15); implementation not mesh-independent (p. 17); SHG intractable, heuristic used (p. 14); regularizing effect unexplained; future: objective/interface trade-off and adaptive refinement in FindStep (pp. 14-15).

method_links.note: NLP trust-region acceptance and radius rules carried to binary control functions; analysis follows a standard trust-region proof strategy.
Losses reported: BTR slower, not mesh-independent, no control dominates on both objective and interface length.

Add a mesh-refinement table (gap, iterations, structural metric) to expose mesh dependence (Table 2, p. 17).

title: Polytopic Superset Algorithm for Nonlinear Robust Optimization
contribution: An inner-approximation algorithm for nonlinear robust optimization with constraints affine in the uncertainty: polytopic supersets dualized by LP duality, refined by cuts, giving feasible iterates, two-sided bounds, feasibility restoration and convergence, faster than Polak's algorithm when robust constraints are many.
problem_entry: Polak's outer approximation gives infeasible iterates and only lower bounds; affine dependence on u enables an LP-duality reformulation (pp. 3, 5).
key_idea: Replace the sample set by a polytopic superset of U, dualize to a finite NLP, shrink by Kelley, projection or gradient-free cuts; phase-I restoration (pp. 7-13).
assumptions: g convex C1, f, h, b C1, U compact nonempty, F bounded (p. 2); affine in u (p. 3); MFCQ (p. 4); convex U as extra assumption vs Polak (pp. 15, 17).
proof_devices: Theorem 2: KKT points of the nonconvex dual reformulation satisfy the first-order condition of the semi-infinite subproblem (p. 8)
Proposition 3: one contradiction with a case per cut type giving uniform separation r/L or r/2R, hence no Cauchy subsequence (pp. 15-16)
Theorem 3: projection gap and error measure vanish on a subsequence (p. 17)
experiments: Julia with filterSQP for all NLPs and Mosek for SDP (p. 17); robust asset allocation with T in {7,14,21} (Table 2, p. 19) and 27 production-cost instances on PJM data (pp. 20-22); CPU-time performance profiles.
positioning: Places itself among discretization, exchange and local-reduction methods and benchmarks against Polak's exchange method (p. 3); extends robust-LP polytopic reformulation [13, 14] to structured NRO (p. 7).
writing: Contrast with Polak stated as feasibility and bounds (pp. 14-15); headline win rate from the performance profile (p. 19); abstract says 'optimal solution' while Theorem 3 gives stationarity (p. 17).
limits_future: Needs convex U and affine-in-u structure (pp. 15, 23); loses some short-horizon runs (Table 2, p. 19); future: relax the affine structure (p. 23).

method_links.note: Same NLP solver (filterSQP) under both algorithms; per-instance tables include losses.
Headline '92% of instances' winner framing, though tied to the many-robust-constraints regime.
Cutting-plane / outer-approximation machinery and phase-I feasibility restoration carried into robust optimization.

Note that convexity is a sufficient condition for global optimality, which means that the two sets of assumptions are not significantly different.

title: Mixed-Integer PDE-Constrained Optimization Sven Leyffer (Argonne National Laboratory)(joint work with Bart van Bloemen Waanders (Sandia National Laboratories), Mirko Hahn…
contribution: Oberwolfach extended abstract (2019 per work-list note) presenting a reduced-space trust-region improvement heuristic for MIPDECO with knapsack subproblems, shown on source inversion and electromagnetic cloaking, with open problems listed.
problem_entry: Mesh-dependent binaries make commercial branch-and-cut prohibitively expensive; two applications (source inversion, cloak design) (p. 1).
key_idea: Linearize the reduced objective, impose an integer L1 trust region (one affine constraint on binaries), solve a knapsack, accept by ActRed/PredRed, halve the radius on rejection (p. 2).
assumptions: Unique PDE solution for each w (reduced space) (p. 1); quadrilateral finite elements (p. 1).
experiments: Qualitative: IoU 82.3% for source inversion (p. 2); cloak figures (pp. 2-3); no baselines.
positioning: Related to NLP trust-region methods and local-branching heuristics for MINLP (p. 1).
writing: Gaps admitted before the closing claim of practical performance (p. 3).
limits_future: Open: bounds-based stopping criterion, multigrid refinement, convergence analysis and mesh-refinement behaviour (p. 3).

method_links.note: NLP trust-region globalization carried into MIPDECO; the unique-PDE-solvability assumption listed in Method 2 limitations appears explicitly.

new_pattern_candidates.pattern: NLP globalization acceptance tests transplanted to non-NLP outer loops
new_pattern_candidates.evidence: ActRed/PredRed ratio and radius halving on a binary trust region

transferable: With binary variables, write the L1 trust region as one affine constraint so the linearized subproblem becomes a knapsack (p. 2).
End a short report with numbered open problems that name the missing guarantees (p. 3).
coauthors: Bart van Bloemen Waanders, Mirko Hahn, Todd Munson, Lars Ruthotto, Meenarli Sharma, Ryan Vogt (joint work; Leyffer presenter)

quotes.text: The presence of mesh-dependent integer variables in these models makes the use of commercial branch-and-cut (see, e.g., [1]) prohibitively expensive (and impractical for 3D extensions of our models).
Despite these gaps in its theoretical justification, the proposed trust-region scheme performs well in practice, and we are working on other applications that could benefit from this approach.

title: Teaching PROFESSOR new math
contribution: CHEP 2018 proceedings (per work-list note) adding to the PROFESSOR event-generator tuning tool a bilevel formulation that replaces manual observable reweighting and a linear-algebra rational approximation that replaces polynomial surrogates.
problem_entry: Manual trial-and-error weighting when the physics model cannot fit all data; polynomial surrogates fail on rational-like data (p. 2).
key_idea: Upper level over simplex weights with mean + lambda*variance of per-observable misfit, lower level weighted chi^2 fit, upper level by RBF surrogate with multistart; rational fits via Vandermonde and SVD null space (pp. 2-6).
assumptions: Surrogates stand in for MC runs (p. 2); invertible Vandermonde ('nicely' chosen points) (p. 5); 1-D presentation (p. 6).
experiments: ATLAS underlying-event data with Pythia8, portfolio vs standard vs random shown only as plots (Fig. 2, p. 4); RBF convergence from two starts (Fig. 1, p. 4); 1-D toy rational vs polynomial (Fig. 3, p. 7).
positioning: Improves the existing PROFESSOR tool [1] for Pythia8/Rivet tuning (pp. 1-2).
writing: Hedged throughout: 'We would argue', 'seems promising', 'looks promising' (pp. 3, 7).
limits_future: Multistart 'not ideal' (p. 3); no quantitative metrics; multi-D rational approximation deferred to an upcoming publication (p. 7).

method_links.note: Manual tuning recast as bilevel optimization, but the upper level is solved by an RBF surrogate with multistart, not his NLP toolkit.
Surrogate functional form changed (rational instead of polynomial) to remove oscillation and nonphysical negative predictions.

transferable: Replace manual reweighting of data groups by a bilevel problem with upper objective mean + lambda*variance of per-group misfit (pp. 2-3).
Fit a rational approximant by linear algebra: square Vandermonde system, denominator from the null space of a small block via SVD (pp. 5-6).
coauthors: Anthony Austin, Steven Mrenna, Juliane Müller, Holger Schulz

quotes.text: We notice that the results have a dependence on the initial guess, which is why we apply a multi-start strategy.
We would argue that in the presence of mis-modelling, the bi-level optimization is able to yield a balanced prediction without human intervention.

title: The Heuristic Static Load-Balancing Algorithm Applied to CESM.
contribution: SC 2013 poster abstract (per work-list note) formulating static node allocation for the CESM climate code as an MINLP solved by MINOTAUR, reporting a 24% speed-up over a baseline guess on 32768 nodes.
problem_entry: A few large tasks of diverse size: dynamic load balancing unsuitable, optimal static allocation NP-hard, practice is 'human optimization' (p. 1).
key_idea: MINLP with nonlinear runtime-vs-processors functions and integer node counts, CESM layout constraints (sequencing, partitioning), solved by MINOTAUR from AMPL (p. 1).
assumptions: Needs accurate benchmarking data and a correct model (p. 1).
experiments: 24% speed-up on 32768 nodes of Intrepid at 1/8 degree resolution vs a baseline guess (p. 1).
writing: Poster abstract; says 'linear optimization technique' after formulating an MINLP (p. 1).
limits_future: Plans a black-box tool, AMPL-to-C++ conversion and release, NCAR pipeline integration (p. 1).

method_links.note: Minotaur used as a solver engine callable from AMPL scripts or C++ code.
MINLP modelling carried into HPC load balancing through a facility collaborator (weak).

transferable: Model processor allocation for a few large heterogeneous tasks as an MINLP whose runtime functions are fitted to benchmark timings, with code-structure requirements as constraints (p. 1).
coauthors: Yuri Alexeev, Sheri Mickelson, Robert Jacob, Anthony Craig

quotes.text: The MINLP approach provides a great flexibility in modeling the allocation problem realistically.
By using HSLB, we improved the speed of CESM on 32768 nodes for 1/8°-degree resolution simulations by 24% compared to a baseline guess on intrepid.
